text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT ▸ spike in 429/503s across embeddings and text-gen clusters · paging eng-oncall · severity: high · link: https://redwood.internal/alerts/ALRT-2170012345

jin kim: noticed a sudden 503 uptick at 16:12 UTC, coincides with a traffic surge from tenant: 'chatly' and a backlog in the prefix cache. dashboards show tail latency jumping.

maya rao: I see the pattern — long queue depth on worker-pool-eu-1 and increased KV cache misses. 429s coming from rate-limiter rejecting concurrent requests.

sam patel: are we seeing one customer causing it or a general spike? quick query: `sum(rate(nginx_5xx[1m])) by (tenant)` shows top source Chatly (49%), internal-batch (20%), others spread out.

maria lopez: paging oncall, what's current mitigation?

jin kim: proposed live mitigations: 1) enable per-tenant soft-ratecap for Chatly to 30 rps for 10m 2) increase worker autoscale threshold on pool-eu-1 3) disable large-batch inference path as fallback. Which should be prioritized?

eli zhang: do soft cap first — that's low-risk and fast. I'll push a ratecap policy change now.

sam patel: +1 on ratecap. also open to surgical disable of reranker for chatly if it continues.

oncall-bot: ACTION: create incident channel #incident-2170012345 — automated logging enabled.

eli zhang: running command:
```
POST https://internal-api.redwood/v1/admin/tenants/chatly/rate_limit
{ "burst": 50, "rate": 30, "duration": 600 }
```
Response: 200 OK — policy applied.

maya rao: metrics after 60s: 429 rate for chatly dropped ~65%, overall 503s down 40%. queue depth trending down. link to updated graph: https://redwood.internal/d/metrics/2170012345

jin kim: good. still seeing some 503s from embeddings-host-04 though — investigating model load.

maria lopez: customer comms? Do we need to notify Chatly support?

sam patel: I'll draft a message: short note that we're throttling to protect service and will follow up with timeline. cc legal/security?

maria lopez: cc customer success. keep it factual: elevated errors observed, mitigation applied (temporary rate limits), ETA next update 30m.

ops-bot: DEPLOY: rolled back reranker-heavy-config on slot varchar-2 in eu region at 16:28 UTC (rollback_id: rb-2170012345).

jin kim: after rollback reranker, 503s reduced further. However we still have spikes coincident with long-context requests (>8k tokens). Suggest enabling prefix-KV caching for that tenant's model variant.

eli zhang: enabling prefix-KV caching for chatly-model-v2 now. command: `infractl cache enable --tenant chatly --model v2 --mode prefix`

maya rao: after cache enable: 95th p50 latency down by 0.9s, errors steady at baseline. good.

sam patel: one risk: caching increases memory usage on instanced hosts. monitor host OOM and eviction metrics.

jin kim: monitoring shows modest memory bump but within headroom; alerted if >85% mem.

maria lopez: customer update sent at 16:40 UTC. response: they saw degraded UX; they appreciate rapid mitigation. asked for postmortem.

jin kim: summary so far in incident channel: root cause likely request spike + reranker heavy path + lack of prefix cache for v2. mitigation timeline: 16:12 detection -> 16:18 soft-ratecap -> 16:28 rollback reranker -> 16:34 enable prefix cache.

eli zhang: next steps: 1) keep ratecap 10 more minutes then gradually lift 2) run targeted replay of chatly traffic on staging to reproduce 3) add an automated rule to pre-warm prefix cache when new high-throughput tenant hits 99th percentile

maya rao: I'll own the dashboard audit — add a dedicated 429/503 breakdown per pool and per tenant, and a widget for top offending routes.

sam patel: oncall handover notes for next shift: ensure soft-ratecap is removed gracefully, confirm OOM-free across eu pool, follow-up with Chatly CS.

jin kim: marking incident as mitigated but not resolved. continuing to monitor for 20m, then promote to postmortem if stable.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE ▸ mitigated · severity reduced to medium · next update scheduled 16:55 UTC.

maria lopez: thanks everyone. please post any follow-up evidence (logs, query snippets) directly in #incident-2170012345. we'll open a Jira for the postmortem.

eli zhang: adding a short runbook action: when chatly or similar tenant exceeds 10k rps over 1m, auto-apply tiered soft-ratecaps (50->30->15) with 5m windows and create incident channel automatically.

jin kim: noted. leaving a quick snippet for runbook: 
```
// apply soft cap
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://internal-api.redwood/v1/admin/tenants/$TENANT/rate_limit \
  -d '{"burst":50,"rate":30,"duration":600}'
```

maria lopez: logging this thread into incident tracker and tagging SRE/Runtime for follow-up. final check: any active customers still seeing errors?

maya rao: last sample at 16:52 shows baseline errors only. closing active mitigation in 8 minutes if stable.

jin kim: thanks team. postmortem owner: maya. action owners: eli (runbook), jin (replay/debug), sam (customer comms).

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated -> monitoring) · final note will be appended after postmortem.
